subject.title: Feature: Add costCurrency config option to customize cost display currency

question: Should OpenClaw add non-USD currency semantics for local configured model costs, and if so should currency live per model, per provider, globally, or only as a display preference?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but adding `costCurrency` changes a high-bar config surface and crosses stored session fields, UI aggregation, status output, and provider-billing semantics that code cannot infer safely.

options.title: Define unit-aware cost contract first
options.body: Choose the currency scope and accounting/display semantics before implementation so local estimates and provider-reported billing stay distinct and consistent.

options.title: Keep local model costs USD-only
options.body: Leave `models.providers.*.models[].cost` as USD per million tokens and document non-USD provider prices as unsupported for local estimates until maintainers approve a broader contract.

options.title: Add display-only symbol preference
options.body: Render a chosen symbol while keeping stored values and telemetry as USD-like estimates, accepting the risk that mixed-currency totals are only presentation-level hints.

recommendation.title: Define unit-aware cost contract first
recommendation.body: Choose the currency scope and accounting/display semantics before implementation so local estimates and provider-reported billing stay distinct and consistent.

likelyOwner.reason: This is primarily a product/config and cost-semantics decision, and the strongest path history points to steipete across usage cost helpers, docs, and recent cost UI work.
